slides.title: From sunlight to useful energy
bullets: Explore the parts of a solar system
Follow energy from generation to storage
Compare two ways to use the output

segments.text: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. This lesson follows the energy through the system and explains the role of storage.

slides.title: Store energy for later
bullets: Stored energy can be used when sunlight is unavailable

segments.text: The battery stores energy for later use. It can supply stored energy when sunlight is unavailable.
First, the panels convert sunlight into electricity. Then the inverter changes the current. Finally, appliances use the electricity.

slides.title: Use now versus store for later
bullets: Direct use supplies appliances while energy is being generated
Battery storage keeps energy for later use

segments.text: Direct use supplies appliances while energy is generated, whereas a battery stores energy for later. The two roles are different.

slides.title: A worked example
bullets: In this hypothetical example, 20% of the generated energy is stored
The remaining energy is used immediately
Actual shares depend on the system and its use

segments.text: Consider a hypothetical example in which 20% of the generated energy is stored. The rest is used immediately. This is an illustration, not a measured result or a typical performance claim.

slides.title: Connect the parts
bullets: Explain how panels, an inverter and a battery differ
Practise distinguishing direct use from stored energy

segments.text: To practise, explain the role of each part in your own words. Then trace the path of the energy and distinguish direct use from storage.
